newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Army buildup seen in northern Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Army buildup seen in northern Sri Lanka.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces appear to be preparing for a long-awaited offensive to establish an overland supply route through Tamil rebel territory to bases in the north, residents in the area said on Friday.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, were also digging in, they said.
"More troops have been moved to the frontline," said a resident in north-central Vavuniya, 220 km (138 miles) north of Colombo. "Equipment has also been moved up by train."

Military officials said security forces were preparing for an offensive to link Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of the capital of Colombo, through the Wanni region, most of which is under rebel control.
All supplies of men and equipment to Jaffna are currently sent by air or sea.
Residents said they had heard unusually heavy gunfire from military bases in Vavuniya late on Thursday. Vavuniya is a garrison town that is the gateway to the Wanni.
"People in the town panicked, thinking that the Tigers had infiltrated and that a fight had started," one resident said.
People who came to Vavuniya from rebel-held areas in the Wanni said guerrilla fighters were on increased alert and were building bunkers in anticipation of an army offensive.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The rebels say the toll is higher.
A spokesman of the LTTE was not immediately available for comment.
